matlab_force_item_rb02.method: For each of the 1,299 cycles of the 102 MATLAB-fixed AB06 phase files, found the AB06 export observation of the same recording, leg and start/end time (1,288 matched; 11 cycles have no export observation: rule A excluded them or they are treadmill steps outside the authors kept set). Forces compared in BW after the sideways sign factor used in the earlier comparison (the MATLAB lateral is lab X; export is outward per leg).
matlab_force_item_rb02.result: 933,959 finite pairs; 918,207 (98.31 percent) within 1e-9 BW; 15,752 (1.69 percent) outside. Exhaustively classified: 15,455 are at samples where the MATLAB vertical force is at or below 1 N (the export sets an unloaded foot with no sign to 0 and its owned vertical to the owned-plate sum; MATLAB keeps plate noise, up to 0.094 BW negative or positive on the treadmill belts); 297 are at contact-edge tails where the MATLAB vertical is 0.02 to 0.11 BW but the export is 0 because ownership ends at the recorded contact interval (levelground 20 pairs per channel, ramp 79). No other difference exists: every sample that is loaded (above 1 N) and inside an owned contact interval agrees to 1e-9. Treadmill vertical agrees in all 277,500 pairs to 1.6e-12. The 5 cycles whose 150 times all fall on the 200 Hz grid agree to 1.9e-3 BW at worst, at the same unloaded samples.
matlab_force_item_rb02.reading: The claim 'matches to 1e-9 off-grid' holds only inside owned, loaded contact. It does not hold where the export applies two stated rules: ownership only inside the recorded contact interval, and zero shear for an unloaded foot. Those are conventions, not data errors, but they replace measured plate readings (noise up to 0.1 BW) with 0. I did not tune anything. RB02 stays done (it was already done; this item was an extra check). The convention is listed for José as a note in the task, not a blocking decision.

missing_force_samples_475592.reading: No sample is missing because plates are missing. Overground: almost all are the heading gate (turning steps). Treadmill: the sign comes from 200 Hz loaded runs, but the vertical force comes from the 1 kHz plate; small blips of 1 N and more (median 0.019 BW, 95th percentile 0.053, maximum 0.24 BW) occur between two unloaded 200 Hz samples, so vertical is finite and the shear is left missing. That is honest (not invented) but it is a two-clock side effect, not a physical heading problem.

rb03_stance.finding: A real problem, not a different definition. On treadmill the RB03 stance is about 0.10 of the cycle for the left leg and 0.60 for the right leg in all 22 participants (median over steps; AB06 left 0.11, right 0.61). On AB06 treadmill_01_01 the left belt stays loaded above 20 N for a median of 139 of 204 samples per left step, while stance_samples is 23; the right leg agrees (126 stance, 127 loaded). So left-leg toe-off events (source events or their pairing with heel strikes) come about 0.4 s too early against the left plate. Overground left steps look fine (levelground stance fraction about 0.57).
rb03_stance.cause: not determined (source left toe-off timing versus the pass pairing).
rb03_stance.downstream: The force mask (stance and under 20 N) and incomplete_stance_force use this stance, so left-leg treadmill masks and flags are too small. Phase and continuous force values themselves, angles, moments, power and counts do not use stance and are unaffected. New task GT21-RB06 opened to find the cause and decide the reexport.
